According to Counterpoint Research, even as overall market shipments declined, Apple still accounted for nearly half of global smartphone revenue in the second quarter. Details below.

Apple posts its highest-ever revenue share in Q2

A new report from Counterpoint Research (cited by MacMagazine) notes that Apple captured 49% of global smartphone revenue last quarter, a historic high, up 22% year-over-year, and the company's highest revenue share for any second quarter on record.

Counterpoint said total smartphone revenue for the quarter grew 7% year-over-year, with Apple the fastest-growing of the top five brands. Its average selling price rose from US$879 a year ago to US$946.

Apple also recorded its highest-ever second-quarter shipment share, climbing from 17% a year ago to 21%; however, the company still ranked second, trailing Samsung, which held 23% of global shipments. Shipment shares fell for the remaining top five brands, with Xiaomi posting the steepest decline, dropping from 14% to 11%, with shipments down 26% year-over-year.

Counterpoint noted that an industry-wide memory shortage forced multiple smartphone makers to raise prices amid rising component costs and tight supply. Apple, meanwhile, kept iPhone pricing largely stable, though Counterpoint expects that to change over the coming quarters.

Original report:

Counterpoint's report was released following Apple's fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call, during which the company warned that supply constraints would significantly worsen in the September quarter, primarily affecting iPhone, iPad and Mac.
